- When sentiment turns bullish (↑) after a downtrend, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After strong sentiment spikes (≥0.67), model often overestimates continuation — apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (↓) after a rally, model underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% to account for mean reversion.
- High news volume correlates with over-forecasting — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each 1.0+ news unit.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — apply 2–5% downward correction.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model underestimates downside — add 1–3% upward bias.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change direction.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) and news is low, model overestimates volatility — reduce forecast by 2–4%.
